answer: The atlas multiplier is published, charged in yarrow, and ivory lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3189 identities would post 724 proofs and burn roughly 44 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
